title: The response contract exposed to the external supervisor matches only what that supervisor consumes
description: Every profile's response is exactly what the supervising system reads and nothing more. HTTP-transport profiles that consume status code only (load balancer, uptime monitor, reverse proxy) return an empty response body with the resolved status code. HTTP-transport profiles that consume a body (Kubernetes HTTPGet, where the kubelet ignores body but operators inspect it during triage) return a minimal JSON body of the shape `{ "status": "pass" }` or `{ "status": "fail" }` with no additional fields. TCP-transport profiles complete the SYN-ACK handshake on pass and refuse the connection on fail. Exec-transport profiles exit with code 0 on pass and a non-zero code on fail. Supervisor-notify profiles emit exactly the notify calls the supervisor expects (for systemd: `READY=1` at startup, `WATCHDOG=1` on the configured watchdog cadence).
rationale: Exposing more than what the supervisor consumes leaks operational surface (dependency names, per-check timings, internal codes) to whichever party can reach the probe endpoint. Load balancers and uptime monitors reach the probe from the public network; a body they never read is a body only the wrong party reads. Kubernetes probes reach from the pod network but the answer is a supervision signal, not a debug surface; richer operator triage sits behind an authenticated dashboard or a separate profile, not on the probe.
